finding.claim: [medium] validateRealm only blocks loopback, link-local, private and unspecified destinations when the realm host is an IP literal. A DNS name such as localhost, or any name that resolves to 169.254.169.254 or an RFC1918 address, passes. The client then sends the user's username/password (Basic auth, or a password-grant form) to that internal endpoint.
finding.source: Bearer realm parameter in a 401 WWW-Authenticate header returned by the registry being contacted (attacker-controlled registry or a server the user is directed to). Precondition: the user has username/password (or refresh token) configured for that registry for the credential-bearing path; the anonymous path yields blind GET SSRF.
finding.sink: Outbound GET to the realm with Authorization: Basic (client.go:422-423) or a POST password-grant form (client.go:470-473) to the attacker-chosen host.

parseChallenge extracts the realm param, unquoted, with no URL or host checks

realm := params["realm"]

url.Parse(realm)

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (226-234) passes https/http. http realm rejected only when the registry is https (229-230). IP-literal private/loopback/link-local/unspecified check (235-242) is bypassed for hostnames. Same-host exemption (238) only matters for IP literals. Origin check at 304 covers the challenge response, not the realm destination. Cross-host public realms are intentional per the doc comment (203-216), so credential forwarding to a public host is by design. Not reviewed: the registry-side network path, and the attacker's TLS requirements for https realms.
finding.repro: Not executed (static review only). Stand up an https registry-like server that answers GET /v2/ with 401 and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="https://localhost:8443/token",service="x". Configure the client with username/password for that host and pull. Expect a GET with an Authorization: Basic header to localhost:8443. Use a DNS name resolving to 169.254.169.254 for the metadata variant. For a plain-http registry, the realm may be http and the request is cleartext.

finding.claim: [low] Descriptor digests taken from registry-supplied manifest or index JSON are interpolated into the request URL path without validation (also blobStore.Fetch at line 752). A hostile registry can make the client send authenticated GETs to other same-host API paths or add query parameters.
finding.source: target.Digest from ocispec.Descriptor decoded from remote manifest/index JSON. digest.Digest is an unvalidated string type. Precondition: the client fetches a manifest or index from a malicious or compromised registry.
finding.sink: HTTP GET to a URL built from the digest, sent with the client's Authorization token or Basic credentials to the same host (auth/client.go:261-291).

trace.note: manifest/index bodies are json.Unmarshal'd (also 1453-1480 for subject indexing)
decodeJSON reads and unmarshals the descriptor-bearing content
manifestStore.Fetch(target) receives the unvalidated descriptor
ref.Reference = target.Digest.String() with no Validate call
AppendRepositoryScope uses the fixed repository, so scope is not derived from the digest
buildRepositoryManifestURL joins base, "manifests" and ref.Reference with "/", no escaping
URL is built with the raw digest string
s.repo.do(req) runs the auth client, which attaches the token or Basic credentials
Do attaches the cached or freshly fetched credential to the same-origin request

finding.guards_checked: ParseReference and Reference.Validate (reference.go:119-223) run only on caller-supplied references, not on descriptor digests. digest.Validate is used only in referrers.go:108 (buildReferrersTag). The response is checked only after it arrives: verifyContentDigest (repository.go:1151) and content.ReadAll in the out-of-tree content package. Requests are GET-only and same-host, so the blast radius is limited to paths the token already reaches. The response is verified or discarded, so there is no cross-host exfiltration. Not verified: the out-of-tree content.ReadAll behavior.
finding.repro: Not executed. Serve an OCI index from a hostile registry whose manifests[0].digest is "sha256:<64 hex>/../../<other-repo>/manifests/latest", or contains '?' or '#', then call Fetch on that descriptor. Expect the GET to target the injected path with the client's Authorization header.

finding.claim: [low] buildRepositoryBlobMountURL interpolates fromRepo into the query string with fmt.Sprintf and no escaping. A fromRepo containing '&' or '=' injects extra query parameters into the cross-repository mount POST.
finding.source: fromRepo argument to blobStore.Mount / Repository.Mount (repository.go:314, 795). Precondition: the calling application builds the source repository name from untrusted input.
finding.sink: POST to the registry's blob-mount endpoint with attacker-shaped query parameters (mount=, from=).

http.NewRequest(POST, url) and do

finding.guards_checked: fromRepo is not run through ParseReference or repositoryRegexp. The scope string built from it (802-803) is not escaped either. Registry-side authorization for the mount source and token scope checks are the backstop. buildReferrersURL (url.go:106-111) uses url.Values, so this is inconsistent. Fix: build the query with url.Values.
finding.repro: Not executed. Call Repository.Mount with fromRepo = "x&mount=sha256:<digest>&from=victim/repo" and inspect the request URL.

finding.claim: [low, logic] Login validates credentials with Ping using a caller-supplied *auth.Client that shares a Cache. A token cached from an earlier session can make Ping succeed without the new credential being checked, so unverified credentials get persisted.
finding.source: cred argument to Login. Precondition: the caller passes an explicit *auth.Client with a non-nil shared Cache, and the cache already holds a token under the empty-scope key for this registry (e.g. from an earlier successful login or anonymous ping).

trace.note: reg.Client is *auth.Client, so authClient = *client copies the Cache field
authClient.Credential = StaticCredential(..., cred)
regClone.Ping(ctx)
Ping calls r.do(GET /v2/), which uses the auth client
Do: cache.GetScheme(host) returns bearer
GetAllScopesForHost returns no scopes, so key is ""
cache hit attaches the cached old-session bearer token; no fetch uses the new credential
store.Put persists the new credential after Ping returns 200

finding.guards_checked: The nil-client path sets Cache=nil (registry.go:42), so the default path is safe. The explicit-client path reuses the shared Cache, so Ping's success is not proof that the new credential is valid. Not verified at runtime. It depends on the registry returning 200 for /v2/ with a cached bearer token, and on an empty-scope token being cached.
finding.repro: Not executed. With a shared auth.Client and Cache: log in successfully once (caches the "" key token), then call Login with a wrong password. Expect Ping to succeed and the wrong credential to be stored.
